## Background

![Reactions studied in Experiment 3: rotational barrier of ethane (3a) and methanol (3b), a conformational change of butane-1,4-diol (3c), and the cis–trans isomerization of pent-2-ene (3d). Carbon is black, oxygen red, hydrogen white; dotted lines are hydrogen bonds.](../images/ex03-reactions.jpeg){fig-alt="Ball-and-stick and line drawings of the four reactions 3a to 3d" width="480"}

In this experiment you will analyze four reactions found in most introductory organic chemistry textbooks. For **3a** you will calculate the energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane. For **3b** you will do the same for methanol. For **3c** you will look at a change of conformation in butane-1,4-diol, which breaks an intramolecular hydrogen bond. **3d** is the isomerization of *cis*-pent-2-ene to *trans*-pent-2-ene. The molecules come from the BHROT27 [@goerigk2017], BUT14DIOL [@kozuch2014] and FH51 [@friedrich2013; @friedrich2015] subsets of the GMTKN55 database [@goerigk2017].

The methods are:

- **LSDA:** SPW92 [@slater1951; @perdew1992; @perdew2018]
- **GGA:** BP86 [@becke1988; @perdew1986; @perdew1986a], BLYP [@becke1988; @lee1988], PBE [@perdew1996] and PBE-D4 [@perdew1996; @caldeweyher2017; @caldeweyher2019]
- **meta-GGA:** SCAN [@sun2015] and B97M-rV [@mardirossian2015; @mardirossian2017rv]
- **hybrid GGA:** B3LYP [@vosko1980; @becke1988; @lee1988; @becke1993; @stephens1994], B3LYP-D4 [@caldeweyher2017; @caldeweyher2019], B3PW91 [@perdew1992; @perdew2018; @becke1988; @becke1993; @perdew1992a] and PBE0 [@adamo1999; @ernzerhof1999]
- **hybrid meta-GGA:** M06-2X [@zhao2008], M11 [@peverati2011], MN15 [@yu2016a] and ωB97M-V [@vydrov2010; @mardirossian2016a]
- **Hartree–Fock** [@hartree1928; @hartree1928a; @fock1930; @slater1930]

Use the **def2-TZVP** basis set [@weigend2005] for every calculation.

The reference energies are:

| Reaction | 3a | 3b | 3c | 3d |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ΔE~ref~ (kcal/mol) | 2.73 | 1.01 | 3.29 | –1.15 |

: {.ref-table}

Compute each reaction energy as ΔE = Σ ν~i~ E~i~, with ν~i~ > 0 for products and ν~i~ < 0 for reactants ([units guide](../guides/units-and-errors.qmd)), then the signed error ε = ΔE~comp~ − ΔE~ref~ and the absolute error |ε|.
